claims.text: Commercial direct-to-consumer microbiome test claims mostly lack clinical validation and research substantiation.
Combining short-read and long-read sequencing technologies produces metagenome assemblies with higher N50 values and fewer contigs compared to single-technology approaches.
A random forest classifier trained for predicting Type 2 diabetes failed to generalize when evaluated on an independent cohort from a different geographic location.

evidence.description: Hoffmann et al. (2024) evaluated direct-to-consumer microbiome companies and found that their claims lack clinical validation.
Chen et al. (2022) demonstrated that joint leveraging of Illumina short reads and Oxford Nanopore or PacBio long reads improves assembly contiguity and N50 metrics.
Reitmeier et al. (2020) trained a random forest model for T2D prediction that showed high internal performance but failed on a geographically distinct validation cohort.

limitations.text: This review only highlights an excerpt of available AI methods and applications in microbiome-related healthcare rather than providing an exhaustive overview.
16S rRNA gene sequencing has low taxonomic resolution limited to the genus level and is subject to amplification biases.
Most reported microbiome AI classification studies lack independent validation datasets, leading to unverified generalizability.
Metaproteomics applications are constrained by false-positive peptide matches during database construction.

future_work.text: Adapt general-purpose federated learning platforms to microbiome data to facilitate privacy-preserving multi-center model training under regulatory constraints like GDPR.
Expand the use of cross-regional validation cohorts and multi-omics data integration to counteract geographic and population-level batch effects.
